title.en: Many languages, many headgears: unity in diversity

text.en: A garden has few kinds of plants and needs constant care. A forest has many kinds of plants, trees, animals, birds and insects, and it looks after itself.

More than a thousand languages are spoken across India. Write the word 'mango' in different languages and enjoy the differences.
Look at a currency note: it carries many languages. This shows that people speak many languages in India.
In a forest, diversity helps everything grow stronger. In the same way, diversity makes our country stronger and more self-sufficient.
Headgear shows variety. In Rajasthan men wear a colourful saafa or pagri. In Himachal Pradesh people wear a topi. Headgear tells us where someone is from, what they believe in or what work they do.
Headgear also protects us. Soldiers, construction workers and miners wear helmets to prevent injuries, and helmets are compulsory on two wheelers.
Drums look and sound different in different parts of India: the dhol, tabla, mridangam, pakhawaj, dholak and others. Each is shaped by local culture and materials.
Instruments like the mridangam are used in Carnatic music, and the sitar and shehnai in Hindustani music. Dance forms came from different states.
India shows togetherness. We have different languages, religions, clothing and traditions, yet we live together, supporting each other like threads woven into one strong fabric.
India also looks to the future: scientists launch rockets, farmers use technology, and children learn science with dance and music.

problem.en: Why does diversity make a country strong?

text.en: A forest has many kinds of living things.
They help each other and the forest.
People of many kinds make India strong.

prompt.en: What is diversity and why is it good for India?

requiredIdeas.en: People live together and help each other
A forest is strong because of its variety

points.en: India has over a thousand languages.
Headgear, drums and dances show variety.
Unity in diversity makes India strong.
